title: staged adversarial anchor injector CI hook
author: Asha Patel

description: Context and motivation: We observed transient regressions that only show up under adversarially altered prompts (subtle paraphrases, punctuation swaps, and token-order shuffles). These regressions are high impact for product safety and ranking-quality. This PR adds a staged adversarial anchor injector CI hook that systematically injects controlled adversarial variants into prompt sets during eval runs and surfaces statistically significant degradations to the existing quality gates. Goals: 1) Detect regressions that are brittle to adversarial perturbations without adding significant flakiness; 2) Provide deterministic, reproducible adversarial probes for local dev and CI; 3) Integrate with the existing eval-orchestration and rollback flows so failing anchors can trigger targeted rollbacks or alerting. Summary of changes: Implemented a new hook at eval_harness/hooks/adversarial_injector.py with a pluggable injection pipeline: sampler -> perturbation layers (paraphrase, token-swap, punctuation-attenuation) -> severity scheduler -> provenance tagger -> replay stub. Added a small, explicit config schema (eval_harness/configs/injector_schema.yaml) to tune budgets (injections per thousand prompts), severity tiers (low/medium/high), deterministic seed behavior for reproducible CI runs, and backoff for flaky prompts. Hook registration added to ci/hooks.yml with two activation modes: nightly-eval (default enabled) and pr-smoke (opt-in via label). Tests: tests/test_adversarial_injector.py includes deterministic fixtures, seed control, and a synthetic eval that asserts no false positives on a stable baseline and high sensitivity on a deliberately weakened model. Integration points: added lightweight provenance tagging in orchestrator/replay_manager.py so failing anchors attach metadata to alert events and rollback candidates. Metrics: included new quality_events adversarial_injector_failure metric emitted when an injected anchor crosses the configured degradation threshold. Rollout and safety: the hook runs in staged mode by default (low severity) for PR smoke and escalates to medium for nightly-eval. The hook records an evidence bundle (sample inputs, model outputs, perturbation pipeline) to S3 with retention controlled by ops config. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of injection pipeline and scheduler - [x] Config schema and default tuning - [x] Deterministic unit tests and limited-integration smoke test - [x] CI registration and docs - [x] Metrics emission and alert mapping - [x] Performance sanity check (mean eval time increase < 6% on nightly config) Commits summary: see commits array above. Small diffs/examples: adversarial_injector.py exposes class StagedInjector with run_batch(batch, severity) and attach_provenance(event_id) methods. Unit test snippet validates seed: assert injector.run_batch(copy_of_batch, seed=42) == repeatable_outputs Review conversation summary: Miguel Ramirez: "Great direction — can we avoid adding high-volume S3 writes by default? Prefer storing only a compressed evidence snapshot and metadata." Asha: "Agree; changed to compress evidence and only upload when degradation passes threshold. Updated docs to clarify storage policy." Sofia Chen: "Can you add a lightweight perf microbenchmark to ensure peak memory of the injector is bounded? Also remove some verbose debug prints." Asha: "Added microbenchmark and fixed logging. Memory increase measured at ~2.7MB per worker on a 2560 batch test." Liam O'Connor: "Test coverage looks good. Only ask is to make PR-smoke opt-in via label rather than a flag to reduce surprise runs." Asha: "Made PR-smoke opt-in via label pr/adversarial-smoke. CI registration updated." CI history: initial run showed lint error (E231) on a helper function, author pushed fix, rerun passed. Unit tests passed on linux/py39 and macos/py310 runners. Nightly integration matrix (staging) passed with one transient failure due to unrelated artifact timeout; rerun cleared it. Final CI status: all checks green. Risk and mitigations: false positives are a concern; mitigated by staged severity, cohort anchoring, and requiring cross-seed confirmation before triggering an auto-rollback. This PR adds a new metric but does not change core gating thresholds by default. Ops and runbook: docs/ops/anchor-injector.md details how to tune budgets and remediate alerts; included runbook steps for evidence retrieval and rollback. Merge outcome: approved by Miguel Ramirez and Sofia Chen, squashed and merged into main via squash merge on 2025-11-12. Follow-ups: ENG-8743 (automated backfill of historical prompt sets against the new injector), ENG-8799 (alert tuning and escalation playbook).
